name: Haggai
title: The Prophet Who Rebuilt the Temple
summary: Haggai was one of the first prophets after the Babylonian exile. He encouraged the people in Judah and the governor Zerubbabel to rebuild the temple in Jerusalem, which had lain in ruins since Nebuchadnezzar's destruction in 586 BC. His prophecies focused on God's promises of blessing if the people prioritized the Lord's house.

keyEvents.title: Call to Rebuild the Temple
keyEvents.description: Haggai delivered God's word to Zerubbabel and the high priest Joshua, telling the people to stop prioritizing their own houses and begin rebuilding the Lord's temple.

keyEvents.title: The People's Obedience
keyEvents.description: Zerubbabel, Joshua, and all the rest of the people listened to Haggai's prophetic message and began the work of rebuilding the Lord's house.

keyEvents.title: The Glory of the New Temple
keyEvents.description: Haggai prophesied that the glory of the new temple would be greater than that of the former one, and that the Lord would bring peace to this place.

keyEvents.title: Blessing After Disobedience
keyEvents.description: Haggai explained that the people's material difficulties were due to their neglect of the temple, but that God would now bless them from the day they began the work.

keyEvents.title: The Promise to Zerubbabel
keyEvents.description: Haggai conveyed God's special promise to Zerubbabel that he was chosen as the Lord's signet ring, a messianic promise linked to David's royal line.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the Book of Ezra
keyEvents.description: Haggai is mentioned together with the prophet Zechariah as among the prophets who encouraged the Jews to rebuild the temple in Jerusalem during King Darius' reign.
